answer: An auditor observes identity binding through a trellis. Each account publishes a lattice of commitments, one per activity type, validated against a cipher only the key holder can open, and its hash is anchored to a per-epoch crystal that changes every round. Violations are recorded when a slot stays empty across epochs while the account still claims rewards for that activity, the signature of a rented key. Because the trellis is per-identity and per-activity, copying a whole lattice to a second account yields duplicate ciphertexts the ledger rejects.
